opening.argument: The offer presents a direct money-to-return proposition: the speaker says, “I paid 240 rubles” under a two-day tariff and “received profit of 20%,” while the Crypto Pay page advertises plans returning 20%, 35%, and 60%, alongside rapid withdrawals. The speaker urges viewers to “try” the project to earn money and directs them to a referral-linked page offering a 50% refback. Those promotional claims are not validated by the displayed account profit, payout, or payment records; they show figures, but do not independently establish that the advertised returns were genuine or available to viewers. The evidence is further compromised by conflicting payment statements, including “this project has not paid” and a separate claim of paying 200 RUB. The conclusion therefore rests on the promotional promise of converting deposits into returns, not verified successful transactions.

citations.quote: I paid 240 rubles. I invested according to the first tariff plan, this is for 2 days. And I received profit of 20%, ie 40 rubles.
I recommend this project to earn in the Internet, try it, and get a good price.
As we see, this project has not paid.
